title: Consul Service Discovery
description: Learn to use HashiCorp Consul for service discovery in microservices environments.

data.text: HashiCorp Consul is a popular service mesh and service discovery tool used by companies like Shopify, Uber, and GitHub. It provides service discovery, health checking, and a key-value store for configuration.

Consul runs as a cluster of servers that maintain the service registry. Services register with Consul using an agent running on the same host. Consul agents forward registrations to the servers and cache query results locally.

data.title: Consul Components
items: Consul Server: Maintains the service registry and replicates across the cluster
Consul Agent: Runs on every node, forwards registration and health checks
Service Catalog: Stores service instances and their health status
Key-Value Store: Stores configuration and feature flags

data.text: Services register with Consul using DNS, HTTP API, or configuration files. Consul performs active health checks to ensure only healthy instances are returned in queries.

data.title: DNS Interface
data.text: Consul provides a built-in DNS server, so you can discover services using standard DNS queries like user-service.service.consul without any client library.

items.question: How does Consul compare to Eureka?
items.answer: Consul offers richer features like health checking, KV store, and service mesh. Eureka focuses on service discovery with simpler semantics but no built-in mesh capabilities.

items.question: Do I need a Consul agent on every node?
items.answer: In production, yes. The agent handles local health checks and caches queries, reducing load on the server cluster.

items.question: Can Consul replace a message broker?
items.answer: No. Consul is for service discovery and configuration. For messaging, use Kafka, RabbitMQ, or similar message brokers.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Consul provides service discovery, health checking, and KV store
DNS interface enables zero-code service discovery
Agents cache results for low-latency queries
Consul is widely used in non-containerized environments
data.takeaway: Consul is a mature, feature-rich choice for service discovery in diverse infrastructure environments.
